interface.switch: SS-01GL13 solder-lug switch in trigger_holder; original EVT-A contact coordinates, no daughter PCB

contact.GL13_contact: R1.3 simulated roller / formed stainless lever, not a rotating wheel
contact.contact_evidence: Omron SS datasheet p6: lever width3.6, unmarked tolerance±0.4. The lever bridges the recess laterally; exact contact still requires a sample check.

side_access_keepout.reason: side-loaded nuts and visual access; not proof that a long axial hex driver fits behind the installed switch

calibration: Install both M2 nuts before the M2x10 screw; slide the fixed nut through the +Y side port.
Leave the +Y trigger gate off and connect the touch wire only after setting. Install the trigger and spring; test with a 1.0 mm gauge at the spring-seat stop.

Fully release; withdraw the trigger and spring through the open +Y side. Adjust the screw outside the frame with an ordinary 1.5 mm hex driver; 1/8 turn is 0.05 mm for M2x0.4. Reinstall and repeat until NO just closes with the 1.0 mm gauge.
Withdraw again; hold the hex driver to preserve the setting and use a thin 4 mm nut wrench (thickness<=1.8 mm) to tighten the front nut against the trapped rear nut. Reinstall the trigger and spring.
After locking, repeat from fully released: 0.8 mm gauge must close, 1.2 mm gauge must stay open.
Remove gauge; verify full-press closure and immediate release opening; install the +Y gate and connect the touch wire; repeat both gauge checks and free return.

axial_driver_boundary.range_note: delta in [-1.5,2.0]; at the 1mm gauge the worst gap is only1.3mm. An ordinary long L-key must not be used in place.
axial_driver_boundary.method: remove and adjust trigger outside the frame, then reinstall and check

lightweight_blade.preserved: slide bars, return tooth, spring bore, screw/nut seats, touch wire channel, cover recess

interface.parking_anchor_boundary: Use a nearby nonfunctional outside blade surface after checking the exact face; do not touch slide/stop/foil/nut/spring surfaces
interface.boundary: resin fit, printed nut-slot grip and actual switch adjustment require first-sample verification
